subject: Peak launch capacity & surge-credit tiering proposal
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyplay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Peak launch capacity & surge-credit tiering proposal

Elena — attaching a concise proposal that tries to balance predictable unit economics with runway for your launch-week spikes. Key highlights up front: 

- 6-month committed program with month-over-month step-ups (you can push more capacity into any month with 72h notice)
- Per-token generation rate tiers (dedicated monthly bucket, float to cover steady-state), with a separate embeddings bucket priced at a lower unit cost
- Launch surge credit pool: we reserve a small buffer of tokens each month to absorb week-of-launch traffic above committed rates; overage beyond credit pool billed at a capped surge rate
- True-up each month, quarterly reconciliation, and a 30-day invoice term to match your procurement request (we can adjust)

I summarized the numeric proposal on page 2 of the attached PDF (SkyPlay_Redwood_Commit_Proposal_Q4-2026.pdf). Quick summary table:

Month 1 (pilot): commit 150M tokens @ $0.00110/token; 20M surge credit at capped $0.00190/token
Month 2: commit 300M tokens @ $0.00095/token; 30M surge credit at $0.00175/token
Month 3+: commit 600M tokens/month @ $0.00080/token; rolling surge credit 50M at $0.00150/token

Optional early-bird: if you sign and enter production by Dec 15 we can apply a 12% introductory discount on the first 3 months (reduces rates shown above).

Open questions for us to resolve before procurement: how you want embeddings invoiced (pooled vs dedicated bucket), whether procurement needs a separate SOW/statement of work line items for the launch engineering support, and whether you want a hard cap on monthly spend.

I've also attached an appendix (RDW_Surge_Modeling_Appendix.xlsx) showing example traffic shapes and expected overage exposures for the proposed surge pools. If you want, we can convert this into a per-week ramp for your feature rollout window.

Would you be open to a short call tomorrow to walk the table? If not, tell me best time and we'll coordinate.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

Attachments: SkyPlay_Redwood_Commit_Proposal_Q4-2026.pdf (proposal, 6 pages); RDW_Surge_Modeling_Appendix.xlsx (model outputs)

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyplay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@skyplay.com, legal@skyplay.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Peak launch capacity & surge-credit tiering proposal

Logan — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear deck. A few quick clarifying questions from our end: 

1) Embeddings: we have two heavy consumers (search indexing and recommendation signals). Would you recommend a separate monthly embeddings bucket or can embeddings be carved out of the committed generation tokens at a lower rate? Procurement prefers a single invoice line if possible.

2) Surge protection: we like the idea of a capped surge rate, but can you guarantee a hard spend cap (e.g., fail closed at $X/day) or would that introduce request throttling? Our ops team cannot have silent throttles in the middle of a live rollout.

3) Procurement asks: 30-day net is okay; they will want SOC2 attestation and an initial security questionnaire answered. Legal also wants to see cancellation windows and an SLA credit matrix.

If you can respond by end of day Thursday we can brief execs next week. Also looping procurement/legal so they can add specifics.

—Elena Ortiz
VP, Platform Ops | SkyPlay Interactive
elena.ortiz@skyplay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyplay.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Peak launch capacity & surge-credit tiering proposal

Elena — appreciate the speedy review and great questions. Quick answers and a suggested alternative that matches procurement's single-line invoice preference: 

1) Embeddings: we can offer an embeddings sub-rate while still billing to a single invoice line. Practically we create an internal accounting bucket so the unit cost for embeddings is $0.00045/token (vs generation $0.00080 in Month 3+), but the invoice will show a consolidated "Committed tokens" line with per-token blended rate and a short appendix showing the internal split for your finance team.

2) Hard spend cap vs throttling: we can implement an active spend cap with a policy that (a) will signal your ops team at 80% usage, (b) will fall back to a pre-agreed degraded throughput mode rather than abruptly dropping connections, and (c) will never silently drop 200 OK requests — you'll get explicit 429s and a clear header indicating throttling and reason. If you need guaranteed zero throttles we can provide a carveout for Dedicated capacity (but that'll increase committed price).

3) Security & SLA: SOC 2 Type II report and our standard SLA matrix are attached in the procurement bundle we share with customers; I'll add the SLA credit matrix into the DocuSign package if that helps. Cancellation: standard 30-day notice after the initial 6-month committed period; early termination fees apply within the initial term as laid out in the SOW.

If these look fine I'll ask Ben to draft an alternate pricing column that uses a blended invoice line and shows the internal split. Then we can circulate a redline.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyplay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Peak launch capacity & surge-credit tiering proposal

Elena — attaching a redline (SkyPlay_Redlines.docx) and an alternate pricing scenario in the same package. Notes on the alternate: 

- Blended monthly invoice line as Marissa suggested (shows blended per-token price but we include an "operational appendix" to separate embeddings vs generation)
- Early-bird modification: 15% discount on Month 1 and Month 2 if you commit to the 6-month plan and start production before Dec 10; we modeled this in the PDF and it reduces your expected overage spend by ~28% under the traffic shape you shared.
- Surge credits: we include a hard monthly credit pool; any traffic above the credit pool is billed at capped surge rates and subject to a daily spending soft-limit. If you want a hard daily dollar cap we can add that as a procurement-only addendum (it requires a slightly higher per-token baseline).

I'm also including a short "engineer on-call" line item for the launch week (4 hours/day handoff monitoring) which we can pick as professional services or include as a credited service if you prefer.

Attachments: SkyPlay_Redlines.docx

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyplay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Peak launch capacity & surge-credit tiering proposal

Team — reviewed your redline with procurement and legal. We're comfortable with the blended invoice approach, the embeddings sub-rate, and the capped surge-rate with the engineered degraded-throughput behavior (we do not want silent data loss). Procurement asked that we document SLA credits explicitly in the DocuSign packet; legal removed two small clauses in section 5 (marked in your redline) but otherwise green.

Next steps: 
- Please send final DocuSign (procurement needs the SLA credit table and Net-30 term clearly visible)
- We'll sign and return by Wed if the packet matches the redline
- Please confirm engineer-on-call hours and whether those are credited or invoiced separately

Thanks — excited to get this live for our holiday launch.

—Elena Ortiz
VP, Platform Ops | SkyPlay Interactive
elena.ortiz@skyplay.com

Attachments referenced: DocuSign packet pending (link provided), SkyPlay_Redlines.docx
